The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{2\pi }{5}-0=\frac{2\pi }{5}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{2\pi }{5}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{2\pi }{5})}=\frac{5}{2}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $\frac{5}{4}$ units up. Hence, $D=\frac{5}{4}.$

Therefore, $B+D=\frac{5}{2}+\frac{5}{4}=\frac{15}{4}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{5x}{2})+\frac{5}{4}.
$$
